quiz_title: 🧠 الذكاء الاصطناعي للصغار - PicToBlox with AI - Challenge 2

questions.question: What are facial landmarks in computer vision?
options: Specific coordinate points tracked on a face (like eyes, nose, mouth corners, and jawline)
questions.explanation: Correct! Landmarks are specific skeletal coordinate dots mapped onto facial features.

questions.question: How many landmark points are typically tracked on a human face by standard AI systems?
questions.explanation: Excellent! Advanced AI face meshes map 68+ coordinate landmarks to track fine details.

questions.question: Which landmark point should a funny mustache filter sprite track to align perfectly above the mouth?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Positioning the mustache at the nose tip or mouth center landmarks ensures authentic alignments.

questions.question: Which block checks if a player is smiling or displaying a happy emotion?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The expression block checks if active facial muscle configurations match 'happy', returning true/false.

questions.question: Which of these emotions can the PicToBlox AI Face Detection identify?
questions.explanation: Great! The AI analyzes muscle structures to identify basic human emotions: happiness, sadness, anger, surprise, etc.

questions.question: How is Machine Learning different from standard pre-programmed coding?
options: Instead of writing fixed rules, we feed the computer data/images so it learns how to recognize patterns itself!
questions.explanation: Excellent! Machine Learning trains algorithms on datasets to discover rules dynamically, mimicking natural learning.

questions.question: Which block is called to analyze camera feeds for everyday items (like bottles, cups, or laptops)?
questions.explanation: Perfect! 'analyze image for object' scans frames for general everyday objects from pre-trained datasets.

questions.question: How can you count how many cups are sitting on your desk using Object Detection?
options: Use the 'get count of detected objects' block
questions.explanation: Spot on! The count block returns the integer count of identified objects on stage.

questions.question: Which block returns the label name (like 'cup' or 'person') of the first detected object?
questions.explanation: Great! The 'get name of object' block returns the category label string identified by the scanner.

questions.question: If you want a label sprite to print out the emotion of the user, what block combination should you write?
options: set label text to (get face X)
set label text to (get face expression)
questions.explanation: Perfect! Setting text to 'get face expression' dynamically prints the active emotion string.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to check if the face expression is happy, and if so, say 'Great smile!'.
questions.task_hint: if is expression happy? then say 'Great smile!'
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Combining expression checks with conditional branching creates smart, interactive emotion readers!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to analyze a camera frame for objects, and say the name of the first detected item.
questions.task_hint: analyze image for object -> say (get name of object 1)
questions.explanation: Perfect! This simple script creates a fully functioning real-time object identifier!
